- Overestimate prices after sentiment spikes (especially +1.00 or high positive sentiment) — reduce forecast peak by 2–5%.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is consistently low or negative (e.g., -0.67 or 0.00) — add 1–3% to forecast to account for mean reversion.
- Forecast tends to lag 1–3 days behind true price movements — adjust forward by 0.5–1.5% per day for recent sentiment-driven momentum.
- Avoid overreacting to short-term sentiment swings — if sentiment shifts sharply, don’t adjust forecast by more than 3% unless confirmed by 2+ consecutive days of similar sentiment.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overpredicts mid-term price peaks — cap forecast at 1.5–2.0% above recent 7-day average to avoid overshoot.
- If sentiment history shows alternating high/low cycles, model tends to overfit to recent highs — apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-period moving average) to forecast.
